title: A Fall River 911 call said a man had killed his parents and had children hostage. It turned out to be a hoax.
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: A 911 call in Fall River falsely reported a murder and hostage situation on Stafford Road.
Police established a perimeter and deployed emergency units before determining the call was a hoax.
Authorities are investigating to identify and hold the caller accountable for the false report and associated costs.

title: Police to increase patrols downtown amid safety concerns, neighborhood group says
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Boston police to increase patrols downtown after high-profile violent incidents, including shootings and assaults, raised safety concerns.
Downtown Boston Neighborhood Association co-founder credits previous public safety summit with improvements but notes recent regression.
Efforts to boost police visibility face challenges due to Boston Police Department staffing shortages, currently 400 officers below minimum.

title: All four ‘Lord of the Rings’ movie Hobbits explored Boston together this weekend
author: Lauren Daley
bullets: 'Lord of the Rings' actors Sean Astin, Elijah Wood, Dominic Monaghan, and Billy Boyd explored Boston during Fan Expo.
The quartet dined at La Royal Cambridge and visited Neptune Oyster and The Green Dragon while in Boston.
They reunited for a '25 Years of Lord of the Rings' event at Fan Expo Boston, highlighting their enduring friendship.

title: Jaylen Brown to host free Boston block party at Boston Common on Aug. 30
author: Annie Jonas
bullets: Jaylen Brown will host '741 Frequency Fest' on August 30 at Boston Common as a farewell to fans.
The event from 2 p.m. to 7 p.m. includes music, games, giveaways, and is free for all attendees.
Brown was traded to the Philadelphia 76ers after 10 seasons with the Celtics, ending his time in Boston.

title: Patriots reportedly releasing 2024 third-round pick Caedan Wallace
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: Patriots are reportedly releasing Caedan Wallace, 2024 third-round pick, drafted 68th overall from Penn State.
Wallace played 10 games over two seasons, with a significant drop in playing time to eight snaps in 2025.
Release of Wallace reduces 2024 draft picks on the roster to two: Drake Maye and Marcellas Dial Jr.

title: Comedian Matt Rife throws down with a paranormal investigator over ‘haunted’ event in Salem
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Comedian Matt Rife faced backlash after allegedly telling a paranormal investigator to commit suicide on social media.
Rife's comments followed a post about a haunted event in Salem featuring items from the Warren Museum.
Paranormal investigator Chris Mac, who is autistic, and his supporters condemned Rife's comments online.

title: Hunter Henry agrees to a two-year extension with the Patriots
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: Hunter Henry, 31, agreed to a two-year extension with the Patriots worth $16 million, potentially reaching $20 million.
The extension includes $14.5 million in guaranteed money and a $4.2 million signing bonus, per ESPN's Adam Schefter.
Henry has 259 catches and 26 touchdowns since joining the Patriots from the Chargers in 2021.

title: 83-year-old drives Jaguar into Acton CVS, causing major damage
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: An 83-year-old woman drove her Jaguar into a CVS in Acton, causing significant damage.
No injuries were reported among the driver, passenger, shoppers, or employees during the incident.
The store will remain closed for repairs; police seek to suspend the driver's license.

title: Logan runway closure this fall could mean more flight delays
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Logan Airport's Runway 27 will be closed for 75 days starting August 31 for a major safety project.
The project involves installing an EMAS system to safely stop aircraft overruns using lightweight materials.
Runway closure may cause flight delays and shift increased air traffic over surrounding communities.

title: One dead, 3 injured in head-on crash on the Cape
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A head-on crash in Sandwich, Massachusetts, on Sunday night left one person dead and three others injured.
The crash involved a 2011 Toyota Prius and a 2017 Toyota RAV4 on Farmersville Road around 8:50 p.m.
The Prius driver died at Cape Cod Hospital; three RAV4 occupants were treated for nonlife-threatening injuries.
